clue.text: Sports car crosses green light, a right little racer

indicators.note: the sports car spans across, so its letters are placed either side of the next pieces

parts.note: GT (gran turismo) is a common badge for a sports car
OK is a go-ahead, the same as giving the green light

explanation.surface: A sports car jumps a green light in a reckless dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open motorised kart is a miniature racing vehicle, so a little racer fits as a description.

clue.text: Good group — it is providing organ for vocalist?

parts.note: a lot is a set or batch, as at an auction
'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A band member insists the group is serving up a singer's needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this part of the larynx is only loosely an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening between the vocal cords in the larynx is the part a singer depends on, hence an organ, loosely, of the voice.

clue.text: Bear put down, unfortunately cut short

parts.note: KO, a knockout, puts an opponent down on the canvas

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A bear had to be put down, its life sadly ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial is popularly called a bear, though it is no relation of true bears.

clue.text: Rolls Royce's gathering is great for spin doctors

indicators.note: gathering means the car's letters gather in and enclose the shuffled piece

parts.note: RR is the badge of Rolls Royce, with the 's supplying an S

indicators.note: sent for a spin, the letters of is great are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Spin doctors like a Rolls Royce assembly because it looks impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctors' reads as one phrase, but 'spin' joins 'for' as the anagram signal, leaving 'doctors' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of senior doctor in training below consultant.

clue.text: Starts to use poems he copied in a stack of poetry?

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: aped means imitated or copied

explanation.surface: A poet borrows from his poems and copies them into a pile of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaped up into a pile is the sense, and the word is a poetic archaism, hence 'of poetry'.

clue.text: Top teams regularly wear blue on label in capital city

indicators.note: in means the middle pieces sit inside the city

parts.note: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the piece after the label

parts.note: EMI is a well-known record label

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of wear blue

explanation.surface: Elite football squads in a capital wear blue kit with a label on it.
explanation.definitionFit: England's top football division is the league of the best clubs, so it collectively names the top teams.

clue.text: Occupying closed-down plant

indicators.note: occupying means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Squatters occupying a closed-down factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, matching the closed-down picture, but it is a botanical plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy tubers, also called dasheen in the Caribbean.

clue.text: It's 4 in e.g. 13 13?

indicators.note: in means the pronoun and numeral sit inside the number type

parts.note: thirteen is an example of a prime number
it, with the 's as a link
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A puzzle about numbers asks where four goes in an example of thirteen.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 13 is read twice: first as the number thirteen, a prime, and then as the cross-reference to 13 across, WILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild in the sense of untamed and uncivilised is close to undeveloped or primal.

clue.text: Democratic country's approach over Prospero's library?

parts.note: D abbreviates Democrat or Democratic
UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a mode is a manner or approach

explanation.surface: A democratic nation's attitude to the library of Shakespeare's magician.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero was the deposed Duke of Milan who preferred his books to ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest Prospero says 'my library was dukedom large enough', so his books were his realm.

clue.text: 11 is line A in poem

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a range is a line, as of mountains or products

explanation.surface: A drink is the subject of line A in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink is an example of a drink, entry 11.

clue.text: They think there's more to come than is actually the case

definitions.text: They think there's more to come than is actually the case

parts.words: They think there's more to come than is actually the case
parts.note: describes early biologists who held that the sperm already contains a fully formed tiny creature, so more is to come than really is

explanation.surface: Optimists who always expect more than will actually arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come' carries a sexual double meaning that points to the theory about sperm.
explanation.definitionFit: These were preformationists who believed each spermatozoon held a miniature organism already formed.

clue.text: The bottle needs 'bones' sign

parts.note: Bones, from sawbones, is slang for a doctor, abbreviated DR
to ink is to sign a contract

explanation.surface: A sign seen at a bottle bank reading 'bones' needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor McCoy in Star Trek is nicknamed Bones, from sawbones, slang for a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the bottle means drinking alcohol, so the bottle stands for alcohol.

clue.text: 11 marks 11's fellowship

parts.note: tea is a drink, entry 11
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
spirit, as in whisky or gin, is a drink

explanation.surface: Drinks taken together mark the bond of fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie and collective loyalty within a group are what the phrase means, close to fellowship.

clue.text: Earth removed from handle that's not broken

indicators.note: removed from means the earth letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to wield is to handle a tool or weapon
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: An electrician pulls the earth wire from a handle that still works.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbroken horse is untamed, so 'not broken' in the horse-training sense means untamed.

clue.text: Get a taxi down to a northern area beach

parts.note: cop is slang for get or catch
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Instructions to catch a cab down to a beach up north.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Rio de Janeiro seafront is one of the best-known beaches in the world.

parts.note: a sup is a drink, entry 11

indicators.note: entry 13 twice gives wild wild, a strong signal to scramble the letters

parts.note: entry 12 is the phrase meaning fellowship, used here as letters

explanation.surface: Cross-references stack drinks and fellowship into a wild jingoism.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive flag-waving is the same zeal as overblown national loyalty, so entry 20 defines it.

clue.text: One going home with English bird

parts.note: a passer is one who passes or goes by
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone heading home with an English bird in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Perching birds belong to the songbird order, so the term covers a bird of that group.

clue.text: No public spaces created — arrest is unlikely!

indicators.note: unlikely signals the letters fall into an improbable new order

explanation.surface: A protest where no public spaces were made, so arrest seems unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: Zones closed to the general public are off-limits areas, so they are not public spaces.

clue.text: Stand up or play guitar

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A busker deciding whether to stand up or play guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker or conductor is a stand from which to address a crowd.

clue.text: Smell of gannet's egg, usually somewhat revolting. Thanks Anax and apologies to Pauline for not underlining 'of.

indicators.note: revolting means turned over, so the selected letters run backwards
somewhat means only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: A gannet's egg usually gives off a rather revolting smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing words are the blogger's thanks to Anax and Pauline, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell of something is to hint at it, so to imply or evoke it.

clue.text: Worry is flooding back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: wets is what something flooding does

explanation.surface: A homeowner frets that water is coming back in.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret anxiously is to be in a state of agitation, a colloquial sense of worry.

clue.text: Try to install a government with a very fierce loyalty

indicators.note: to install means the following pieces are set inside the word for try

parts.note: to have a fling at something is to try it

explanation.surface: An attempt to put in a regime that demands fierce loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt, noisy patriotism, waving the national banner, is a show of fierce loyalty.

clue.text: Chinese text that not hard as a decoration

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Chinese text, not a hard one, used as decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugary coating on a cake is a decoration on it, so frosting stands for a decoration.

clue.text: 19's 13 13 location

indicators.note: wild wild is entry 13 twice, signalling a scramble

parts.note: entry 19 is worry, a word meaning to fret, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Where the Wild Wild West is located.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point names a region or position, as in the West, so it is a location.

clue.text: River gorge, but not 26 river

indicators.note: but not means the letter for caught is taken away

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine
entry 26 is caught, and C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A river gorge, but not the one the river was caught in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the major European waterway flowing from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Get out of the way — it's a speed freak

indicators.note: freak signals the letters are distorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A warning to move aside because a speed freak is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving out of someone's path to let them pass is exactly getting out of the way.

clue.text: 22's closed very majestically

parts.note: entry 22 is West, so West's points to Mae West, giving her first name with the S
a door pushed to is closed
so is used to mean very

explanation.surface: Mae West's place was closed very majestically.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was the American film star and wit.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction tells the player to perform in a stately, dignified manner.

clue.text: Got date for hearing

indicators.note: for hearing means the word for date is said aloud

parts.note: to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone got a date for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught as a past tense of catch means obtained or got hold of.
